gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her excellent presentation.
gaps.explanation: 'Compliment somebody on something' means to praise; 'complement' means to go well with.
'Complement' means to combine well with or complete something; 'compliment' means to praise.

gaps.sentence: The comedian was so ___ that everyone cried with laughter.
gaps.explanation: 'Funny' is an adjective describing something that makes you laugh; 'fun' describes enjoyable experiences.

gaps.sentence: One of the screws on the bracket has come ___.

gaps.sentence: I was so ___ when I forgot her name in front of everyone.
gaps.hint: how you feel in an awkward social situation
gaps.explanation: 'Embarrassed' describes short-term discomfort in a social situation; 'ashamed' implies guilt about wrongdoing.

gaps.sentence: This tooth is ___ and will probably fall out soon.
gaps.explanation: 'Loose' is an adjective meaning not firmly fixed; 'lose' is the verb meaning to no longer have.
